quests.instruction: Every swing at the playground is full, and laughter fills the air. When is this most likely happening?
quests.hint: Consider when a playground is warm, bright, and busy.
quests.explanation: Playgrounds are busiest in the daytime, when there is plenty of light for children to see and play safely.
quests.funFact: Playground equipment is often made of rubber and soft materials to keep falls gentle.

quests.instruction: A school hallway is dark and empty, with every door locked. When is this most likely?
quests.hint: Schools are busy while classes are going on.
quests.explanation: School buildings are usually locked and dark at night, after students and teachers have gone home.
quests.funFact: Many schools have a custodian who cleans the building after classes are over.

quests.instruction: A yellow school bus flashes its lights as children with backpacks wait at the curb. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Ask yourself who would be standing outside with backpacks, and when.
quests.explanation: Buses pick children up in the morning to take them to school, when the day is just beginning.
quests.funFact: School buses are painted a special yellow because it is easy to see.

quests.instruction: In a shop window, a baker slides trays of fresh bread from the oven. The street outside is still empty and the sky is only just starting to lighten. What is the most likely time?
quests.hint: Bread has to be ready before shoppers arrive.
quests.explanation: Many bakers start work very early, so fresh bread is ready for people to buy at the start of the day.
quests.funFact: Some bakers begin their work long before sunrise.

quests.instruction: Joggers and dog walkers use the park path while families spread picnic blankets under the high Sun. When is this?
quests.hint: Picnics need good light to see the food and the grass.
quests.explanation: A high Sun and picnic blankets are clear signs of daytime in a park.
quests.funFact: A picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, usually on a blanket in a park or garden.

quests.instruction: A group sits around a small fire on the sand, roasting marshmallows beneath a sky full of stars. When is this?
quests.hint: Notice what the sky looks like around the fire.
quests.explanation: A sky full of stars and the glow of a campfire fit night, when the sky is dark.
quests.funFact: Campfire stories are an old way for people to share news and tales in the dark.

quests.instruction: A crossing guard in a bright vest walks children across the street after the last bell. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: The school day has just ended.
quests.explanation: After the last school bell, children head home, so the crossing guard is helping in the afternoon.
quests.funFact: Crossing guards wear bright vests so drivers can spot them easily.

quests.instruction: In a garden, dew still sparkles on the leaves while the Sun is just rising. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Tiny drops of water gather when the air cools overnight.
quests.explanation: Dew forms on cool nights and is often still on leaves in the early morning, before the Sun dries it.
quests.funFact: Dew is just water vapor from the air turning into tiny drops on cool surfaces.

quests.instruction: Candles glow on restaurant tables as families finish dinner and the sky outside darkens. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Dinner is the meal that closes the day.
quests.explanation: Dinner and a darkening sky show that evening is turning into night.
quests.funFact: The word restaurant comes from a French word that means to restore, because of the meals served there.

quests.instruction: A crowded bus carries workers holding cups of coffee while the Sun is just rising behind the buildings. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Look at where the Sun is, and what people are heading toward.
quests.explanation: Workers commuting at sunrise are heading to jobs for the day, so it is early morning.
quests.funFact: Many people take buses and trains to work so they do not have to drive.

quests.instruction: Children in a bright classroom paint pictures while the school day is half over. Which time of day is it?
quests.hint: Schools are mostly open when it is light.
quests.explanation: Most school lessons happen in the daytime, so art class in a bright classroom fits the day.
quests.funFact: Painting with a paintbrush helps children practice careful hand movements.

quests.instruction: A neon sign flashes over the street, and shop windows glow as people stroll by. When is this most likely?
quests.hint: Neon signs look brightest when the sky is dark.
quests.explanation: Neon signs and shop windows look brightest after dark, when they stand out against the night.
quests.funFact: Neon lights shine because electricity makes a special gas glow inside the tube.

quests.instruction: An ice-cream truck plays its jingle while children line up in the sun with coins in their hands. When is this?
quests.hint: Decide when children are usually out and about with their families.
quests.explanation: Ice-cream trucks drive around neighborhoods in the daytime, when children are playing outdoors in the warmth.
quests.funFact: Ice cream melts quickly in the sun, which is why we eat it fast.

quests.instruction: A family sits on the porch and watches little lights blink above the garden. When is this?
quests.hint: Which time of day makes small lights easy to notice?
quests.explanation: Fireflies blink at dusk and after dark, so seeing them means evening or night.
quests.funFact: Fireflies are not flies at all. They are a kind of beetle.

quests.instruction: A lifeguard sits in a tall chair, watching swimmers in the water, and everyone is wearing sunscreen. When is this?
quests.hint: Lifeguards watch swimmers when they can see them clearly.
quests.explanation: Lifeguards usually watch swimmers during the day, when beaches are open and visibility is good.
quests.funFact: Lifeguards use bright flags to show whether the water is safe.

quests.instruction: Lights glow inside a bakery while the street outside is still dark. A baker is lifting a tray of rolls from the oven. Which time is most likely?
quests.hint: The street is dark, and the bread must be done by the time shoppers come.
quests.explanation: Bakers often work in the early hours before sunrise so bread is fresh for the morning crowd.
quests.funFact: Bread dough needs time to rise, so many bakers start long before breakfast.

quests.instruction: A farmer leads cows to the barn for milking as the Sun peeks over the fields. Which time of day is it?
quests.hint: The Sun is just beginning to appear.
quests.explanation: When the Sun peeks over the fields, the day is just starting, and many farmers begin work early.
quests.funFact: Farmers often start their chores at dawn, since animals need food and care each day.

quests.instruction: Park lamps blink on along the path as the sky fades to purple. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Lamps come on when daylight is leaving.
quests.explanation: Park lamps switch on at dusk to help walkers see as the sky fades to purple at the end of the day.
quests.funFact: Some park lamps are solar powered, charging in the sun and shining after dark.

quests.instruction: A teacher locks the school door and tells the last child, "See you tomorrow!" Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Consider what "See you tomorrow" means about the day.
quests.explanation: Saying "See you tomorrow" means the school day is over, so it is the end of the afternoon.
quests.funFact: In many countries, school ends in the afternoon, so children go home after lunch.

quests.instruction: Bees buzz from flower to flower in a garden while the Sun warms the petals. When is this?
quests.hint: Flowers open and bees fly best in warm, bright light.
quests.explanation: Bees usually visit flowers during the day, when it is warm and bright enough for them to fly.
quests.funFact: A honey bee visits thousands of flowers in a day.

quests.instruction: "We're closing soon," says the grocery clerk as streetlamps glow outside. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Look at the lamps outside.
quests.explanation: Streetlamps glowing while a shop closes means dusk or evening, as the day ends.
quests.funFact: Some grocery stores stay open late, but many close in the evening.

quests.instruction: A bus is almost empty. Reflected lights slide across its windows and the driver yawns at the end of a long day. When is this?
quests.hint: Ask yourself when there are few riders and many lights outside.
quests.explanation: An empty bus, reflected lights, and a tired driver all point to late at night, when the day has ended.
quests.funFact: Night buses help people get home safely after dark.

quests.instruction: "Pack up, class," says the teacher, "the bell is about to ring." The Sun is still high. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: The Sun is not yet low.
quests.explanation: A high Sun and the end of the school day tell us it is afternoon, not evening yet.
quests.funFact: The school bell has been used for centuries to tell people when to start and finish.

quests.instruction: People in sunglasses and hats buy cold lemonade at the park. When is this most likely?
quests.hint: Sunglasses are for something bright.
quests.explanation: Sunglasses, hats, and cold drinks are all things we use when it is bright and warm outside during the day.
quests.funFact: Lemonade stands are a classic way for kids to share a cold drink on a hot day.

quests.instruction: A lighthouse beam sweeps over the dark sea as ships float in the distance. When is this most likely?
quests.hint: Lighthouse lights matter most when it is hard to see.
quests.explanation: Lighthouses help ships find their way in the dark, so their beams are most needed at night.
quests.funFact: Many lighthouses have special lenses that make the beam reach far across the sea.

quests.instruction: The playground lamps are on, the swings sit still, and no one is around. Which time of day is it?
quests.hint: Playgrounds are usually quiet when people are home.
quests.explanation: A lit but empty playground fits night, when families are at home and most children are in bed.
quests.funFact: Some public parks close at night so people stay safe.

quests.instruction: Which place would most likely be empty at midnight?
quests.hint: Decide where people go to sleep.
quests.explanation: At midnight, most people are asleep at home, so bedrooms are in use while school playgrounds are empty.
quests.funFact: Midnight is the moment when one day ends and the next begins.

quests.instruction: Which clue best tells you a bus is traveling in the evening?
quests.correctAnswer: Headlights on and a dim sky
options: Headlights on and a dim sky
quests.hint: Look for a clue about the light.
quests.explanation: A dim sky and headlights point to evening. Lunch boxes are carried at school time, not at the end of the day.
quests.funFact: Buses often have lights inside that switch on when it gets dim.

quests.instruction: Where would you most likely find a family in their pajamas?
quests.correctAnswer: At home, getting ready for bed
options: At home, getting ready for bed
quests.hint: Pajamas are for resting.
quests.explanation: People wear pajamas at home, usually at bedtime, so a family in pajamas is likely getting ready for sleep.
quests.funFact: Some families keep a special pair of pajamas just for holidays.

quests.instruction: Which place is likely to be busiest on a school day at noon?
quests.hint: Consider where lots of children gather to eat in the middle of the day.
quests.explanation: At noon, a school cafeteria is full of students eating lunch. At midnight, schools are usually locked and empty.
quests.funFact: Many school cafeterias serve hundreds of lunches in just an hour.
